reference_rtl: rtl/dsrom_sys/s81_capture_parent/ot_hdc_core_v41x.sv (+ ot_chip_v41x_tile.sv, ot_v41_rt_die_l20_c8.sv: FULL_SHAPE 1, X_ROM 1, SUN 256, SUM 64, HHW 8, VM_AW 19, ROM_R 128): the S81 hub slabs are a physical partition of this core

common_rules.transport: every die bus is a valid-only stream: hub end blocks (ot_meso_fifo / ot_ratio_cdc_fifo) deliver {data, valid} in the receiver's clock; the only die-level flow control is a start block's 3-b status {0, w_live, w_rdy} (xes/xws/qNEs..). A receiving slab accepts one word every cycle and never drops.
common_rules.boundary: every slab is register-to-register: each die input bit is captured in a flop at its pin, each die output bit is launched from a flop at its pin (OWNER 2026-10-06 addendum); slab-internal wires > ~400 um get a register stage.
common_rules.framing: hub buses carry typed in-band frames, no width change: a header beat {type 4, tag 8, op 8, len 12, ...payload} followed by len data beats; the receiver knows the frame length from the header. Types: 1 op descriptor, 2 operand/data beat, 3 result beat, 4 done/status (tag, fault code), 5 fault. Units never stall on their own data (the core's rule: every unit is a fixed pipeline); the VM sequencer issues a unit op only when its wait mask has drained, exactly as ot_hdc_core_v41x.
common_rules.domains: serial 0.9 GHz: VM, SU s/n, HC s/n. stream 1.2 GHz: gather, capture, collective, selector, collector, svc, ctrl (cks; ckh HBM).

decision.arch: TWIN SPLIT (lead decision 2026-10-06 13:50 PT). The unit RTL is NOT modified. The VM slab instantiates an unchanged TWIN of the unit (ot_hdc_v41x_su_adapt+vec / ot_hdc_v41x_he_adapt+hcp) on the VM's read ports; only its read/write ADDRESS, enable and control outputs are used, so synthesis prunes its datapath. The VM pushes the twin's read words (rd_q / x_q, read latency 1 as in the lane's MR->X capture) to the slab over the die bus with a FIXED latency D_f; the slab runs the same unchanged unit with the same op issued D_f cycles later (descriptor on dedicated header bits of the same bus, so both see the same latency) and feeds rd_q from the bus; its own address outputs are left unconnected. Results travel slab->VM as {we, data} only (write addresses come from the twin, delayed by D_f+D_r); the twin's idle/ready/chase completion is delayed by D_f+D_r before the VM sequencer sees it, so wait masks still mean 'written'. Exact by construction (same RTL, deterministic schedule, gather indices read by the twin from the VM). Bench: core-native unit on a behavioural VM vs twin+slab pair with a D_f/D_r pipe, write streams compared word for word; negative controls: D mismatch by 1, one dropped beat, twin idle undelayed.

bus_widths_native_rate.su_to_vm_per_slab_b: 128 x 32 vm data + 128 we + 128 x 32 kv data + 128 kv we + 16 x 32 res data + 16 res we = 8,592
bus_widths_native_rate.die_today: f_vm 1024 in, t_hc 512 out per slab

decision.G2_choice: WIDEN (die count / wires are not scarce; the narrow bus multiplies SU occupancy ~16x: v41x_replay SU busy 10,845 cycles/token at spec lanes, SU depth 28,178 is already the top critical-path item). Generator change for S81-RERUN: vm->su_s/su_n 16,384 b each, su->vm return 8,592 b each DIRECT to the VM (not through HC; HC pass-through dropped), both register-staged every <= 215 um (r9m215 common clock).
decision.latency_cost: every SU op on the critical path gains D_f + D_r (the round trip of the 6.3 mm slab trunk, ~2 x 15 stages at 425 um, plus pin flops): must be priced by COMPOSE per SU dependency; expected well over the 2% pre-approval -> reported, run anyway (the partition is mandatory).
decision.state: DECIDED (remote-read); RTL next phase: lane/controller RD_XLAT
decision.chase_finding: Unchanged-RTL twin is NOT enough when an op chases (su_chase > 0 or CLS_DRAIN): su_adapt chains SELF on the vec's own completion (cr_dseq), and the twin and the slab cannot both see completion at the right time by RET_STAGES alone (slab extra x, twin extra y: arrival needs y = D_f + x + D_r, mirrored release needs y = x -> D_f + D_r = 0). Required RTL change (default-off parameter of ot_hdc_v41x_vec, SPLIT=1): cut the vec at its existing broadcast (BCAST_STAGES) and return (RET_STAGES) pipes -- controller + emit/chain + address-only lanes in the VM slab, data lanes + reducer in the SU slab driven by the broadcast delayed D_f, write data returning D_r, completion (cr_*) counted at VM arrival. Chained ops then stall in the controller only, and both sides see one schedule. Bench: SPLIT=0 vs SPLIT=1 (D_f, D_r in 1..16) inside ot_hdc_core_v41x on the S81 parent programs, VM write stream and outputs word-exact; negatives D mismatch, dropped beat, completion counted at slab output.
decision.chosen: REMOTE-READ (supersedes the twin, lead 14:10 PT): the whole unchanged su_adapt+vec sits in the SU slab; its lanes' VM reads cross the die: rd_addr/rd_re/rd_src (4 x 128 x 24 + 512 + 1,024 b per slab) go SU->VM, rd_q (16,384 b) returns, so the lanes see the read RD_XLAT = 2 x bus stages + 2 pin flops later; writes land at the VM after RET_STAGES = native + bus stages, so cr_* (counted when writes LAND) and chase stay exact with no twin. RTL change (default-off): ot_hdc_v41x_vec already carries RD_XLAT for the KR credit timing but ot_hdc_v41x_vec_lane captures X one cycle after MR and the per-vector control pipe in the controller assumes that; the change is an RD_XLAT delay of the lane's read tags (m_v/m_o/m_par -> x_*) and of the controller's control-pipe taps from X onward, plus the gather path (index read at F0 used at G2: G2 moves by RD_XLAT). go/ready across the die: a 1-op credit in the VM (su_adapt latches one op) and idle delayed by the bus round trip (conservative). Bench: RD_XLAT/RET/BCAST 0 vs split values inside ot_hdc_core_v41x on the S81 parent programs (core outputs + VM write stream word-exact); negatives: lane delay off by 1, control tap not moved, idle undelayed.
